Subject: Marketplace listing billing & SLA questionnaire — Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for starting the marketplace onboarding conversation with Stratus Cloud. As part of the commercial review we need clarifications on billing, metering, and SLA mechanics before we can finalize the listing. Please see the attached questionnaire (aws-marketplace-questionnaire.pdf) and provide answers to the items below:

1) Pricing model and public SKU details (unit, unit_multiplier, currency).
2) Metering type — usage metering vs. fixed subscription, and the expected daily/weekly call volume that drives metering.
3) Billing integration options — whether you will use AWS Marketplace Metering Service or invoice customers directly; if using AMMS, provide your register/ARN and metering dimensions.
4) Refunds / billing disputes process and contact.
5) SLA target (availability %) and credits policy (how credits are computed and applied).
6) Data residency or region limits that affect billing or metering.
7) Any marketplace-specific payment terms we should be aware of (net terms, tax treatment).

We need an initial response within 3 business days; if more time is required, let us know. If helpful, propose a 30-minute sync.

Best,
Maya Chen
AWS Marketplace Ops

Team / AWS / Stratus,

Legal & compliance notes (high level):
- Proposed SLA: 99.9% monthly availability is reasonable for hosted API. For Dedicated we should mark a different SLA; will note as "by contract".
- Credits: propose standard marketplace-crediting approach: for each 0.1% below the SLA, customer receives 2% credit up to a cap of 50% of the monthly bill. Need Sales to confirm cap tolerance.
- Data residency: if Stratus requires region-specific hosting, that does not affect billing but may affect available SKUs and pricing due to regional infra costs (note in listing).
- Metering terms: if using AMMS, Redwood will be responsible for accurate metering events. We should include a dispute window (30 days) and reconcile reports monthly.
- Tax/terms: we prefer net-30 for marketplace settlements where allowed, otherwise follow marketplace payout cycles.

I've sketched the SLA appendix with credit table and sample language (sla-appendix-draft.docx). Ben, please confirm the credit cap and whether we can accept the marketplace payout timing. Priyom, we'll need the AMMS registration metadata and to confirm the dimension naming convention.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Hi Maya / Stratus procurement,

Thank you for the questionnaire — please find consolidated answers below and the requested artifacts attached. If anything needs further detail, flag the item and we'll follow up quickly.

Summary answers (high level):
- Pricing/SKUs: Primary public SKU = redwood-api-gen-1k (unit = 1k tokens, USD). Dedicated/reserved SKU = redwood-dedicated-month (unit = month). See attached redwood-billing-matrix.xlsx for full SKUs and price bands.
- Metering: We will use AWS Marketplace Metering Service (AMMS). Proposed metering dimension: "RedwoodTokens". We will provide registration ARN during onboarding.
- Billing integration: For hosted customers via AWS Marketplace we will utilize AMMS. For dedicated/reserved deals (enterprise) we invoice directly per contract.
- Refunds/disputes: billing@redwood.com is the contact; disputes are reconciled within 30 days and refunds/prorations are applied when appropriate.
- SLA: Proposed hosted API SLA = 99.9% monthly availability. Credit policy: 2% monthly credit for each 0.1% below SLA, up to 50% cap (see attached sla-appendix-draft.docx). Dedicated capacity SLA handled per contract.
- Data residency: We can offer region-pinned deployment for customers with residency requirements; this will affect SKU availability and pricing (noted in the listing summary).
- Payment terms: We prefer net-30 where the marketplace allows; otherwise follow marketplace payout schedule.

Next steps:
1) Maya — please confirm whether the AMMS dimension name "RedwoodTokens" is acceptable and provide the onboarding ARN to register.
2) Stratus procurement — are the proposed credit terms acceptable for the PoC? If you'd like a conference call to walk through the appendix, we're happy to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow morning.
